v7.title: UUID v7 (time-ordered)
v7.description: UUID v7 starts with a 48-bit Unix timestamp in milliseconds followed by random data, so UUIDs sort by creation time. That makes them ideal as database primary keys: they keep chronological order and improve index performance.

v4.title: UUID v4 (random)
v4.description: UUID v4 fills 122 of its 128 bits with random data (the other 6 mark the version and variant), so duplicates are practically impossible. The format is xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-yxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx, where each x is a hexadecimal digit and y is 8, 9, a or b. Use it when you need maximum randomness and sort order doesn’t matter.

about.title: About JWT
about.description: A JSON Web Token (JWT) is a compact, URL-safe way of passing claims between two parties. It has three parts separated by dots: header, payload and signature.
about.header: Metadata about the token, such as the signing algorithm (HS256, RS256…) and the token type (JWT).
about.payload: The claims: statements about the user and any other data. Common claims include sub (subject), exp (expiration time) and iat (issued at).
about.signature: Lets the receiver check that the token has not been tampered with. It is computed from the header, the payload and a secret or private key.
about.security: This tool only decodes tokens; it does not verify signatures. JWT data is encoded, not encrypted, so never put sensitive information in a token. Always verify tokens on the server.

about.hex: Hexadecimal notation: base-16 digits (0–9, A–F) for the red, green and blue values. The usual choice in CSS and design tools.
about.rgb: Red, green and blue channels from 0 to 255, with an optional alpha (opacity) channel from 0 to 1. The standard for the web and digital displays.
about.hsl: Hue (0–360°), saturation (0–100%) and lightness (0–100%), with optional alpha. More intuitive for adjusting colors and building palettes.
about.cmyk: Cyan, magenta, yellow and key (black) ink percentages used in print. The conversion is a simple approximation without a color profile.
